stmtstats.summary: Capture cumulative statement statistics at two moments and rank what changed. PostgreSQL diffs pg_stat_statements by queryid; MySQL/MariaDB diffs performance_schema digests. Read-only captures can also be saved for later comparison.
stmtstats.howToOpen: Insights menu -> Statement statistics (also on the native Tools menu). Renders PgssHistoryPanel on PostgreSQL and MysqlDigestPanel on MySQL as one tab receiving the current session.
keyActions: PostgreSQL: detects pg_stat_statements; offers 'Enable extension' if available but not enabled, or install instructions if absent
Capture snapshot (PostgreSQL keeps the last 12); pick Before and After snapshots
Read the diff - PostgreSQL sorts by delta total time with delta calls/mean/rows and changed/new/gone status; MySQL shows + execs, + total time, avg, + rows examined per digest (top 200)
PostgreSQL: toggle showing statements with no new calls; warns when a counter reset happened between snapshots
Save the latest capture into the persistent digest store and diff any two stored snapshots (DigestStoreSection, both engines)
stmtstats.engines: MySQL/MariaDB (performance_schema digests) and PostgreSQL (pg_stat_statements). Other engines keep no cumulative statement digest, so the menu entry is gated on the stmtStats capability; SQL Server's richer Query Store keeps its own panel.
stmtstats.caveats: Read-only. PostgreSQL needs pg_stat_statements; MySQL needs performance_schema. Capture at least two snapshots with workload between them. A counter reset invalidates deltas and is flagged on PostgreSQL.

pgworkload.summary: Investigate one manual baseline/after window with ranked statement deltas, optional wait sampling and matching local incidents. Statement and incident SQL opens in the editor; there is no always-on collector.
pgworkload.howToOpen: Insights menu -> PostgreSQL Workload (also native Tools > Insights). Available only on PostgreSQL sessions.
keyActions: Capture a baseline, run the workload, then capture After
Optionally sample waits during the measurement; sampling stops on After and on panel close
Read ranked statement deltas with reset/eviction warnings, exact-window wait aggregates and matching local incidents
Insert statement or incident SQL into the editor, or open the full incident timeline
pgworkload.engines: PostgreSQL only, gated by the pgWorkload capability. pg_stat_statements uses the same availability/enable flow as Statement statistics.
pgworkload.caveats: Wait samples are in-memory, capped at 2,000 and cover only time actively sampled while the panel is open; they are not server history. Incidents are limited by the existing local stores' retention. There is no always-on collector or additional snapshot database.

binlog.summary: Inspect MySQL/MariaDB binary-log files and events, then generate a mysqlbinlog point-in-time-recovery command from a chosen position. The recovery command is copied, never executed by TxUI.
binlog.howToOpen: Insights menu -> Binary logs. Renders as the BinlogPanel tab with the current session.
keyActions: Pick a binary-log file from the dropdown (newest selected by default)
Reload the events for the selected file (SHOW BINLOG EVENTS ... LIMIT 500)
Click an events row to fill the start-position from its Pos column
Set start-position and stop-datetime inputs, then Copy command to copy the generated mysqlbinlog | mysql pipeline
binlog.caveats: Read-only in-app; the generated PITR command is never executed - it contains placeholders (<host>/<port>/<user>) that you fill in and run in a shell yourself. Requires a live MySQL connection with binary logging enabled and privileges to SHOW BINARY LOGS / BINLOG EVENTS. Event list capped at 500 rows.

slowlog.summary: Analyze a local MySQL/MariaDB slow-query log offline. Statements are fingerprinted, grouped and ranked by total time in a pt-query-digest style report. No server connection is needed after opening the file.
slowlog.howToOpen: Insights menu -> Slow-log analyzer. Renders as the SlowLogPanel tab.
keyActions: Open slow log... (button) - file picker for .log/.slow/.txt files, read via the read_slow_log backend command
Read the ranked table: statement shape, count, total time, avg, max, rows examined (top 200 shapes)
slowlog.engines: Gated to mysql (menu). Works purely on a local slow-log file - it does not query the server, so any MySQL/MariaDB slow log can be analyzed offline once opened.
slowlog.caveats: Operates on a file, not a live connection; no server round-trip. Results limited to top 200 statement shapes.

documenter.summary: Generate deterministic, commit-ready schema documentation in Markdown or HTML, with an optional relationship diagram. Catalog sections are introspected separately so one missing privilege does not erase the whole document.
documenter.howToOpen: Schema menu -> Documenter. Renders as the DocumenterPanel tab with the current session and selected database (schema).
keyActions: Reload - re-introspect the catalog for the selected schema
Choose format: Markdown or HTML (segmented control)
Toggle 'Relationship diagram' (on by default)
Toggle 'Row estimates' (off by default; opt-in because estimates drift every write)
Copy the document to clipboard
Save... the document to a .md/.html file
Read the on-screen preview and stats (table/routine/foreign-key counts)
documenter.engines: MySQL and PostgreSQL only (gated to sqlDba). MySQL uses information_schema; PostgreSQL uses pg_catalog (format_type, pg_get_indexdef, pg_constraint, etc.). On other engines it shows 'Documenting reads the catalog, so it needs MySQL or PostgreSQL.'
documenter.caveats: Requires a live MySQL/PostgreSQL connection and a selected database. Row counts are optimizer estimates, not COUNT(*). A missing grant on one catalog silently drops that section. MySQL index expressions need MySQL 8.0.13+; older servers fall back to plain columns.

fleet.summary: Compare every server sharing a label with read-only checks. Detect roles from the servers, then review Variables, Indexes and Statistics tabs for configuration drift, index divergence and stale table statistics.
fleet.howToOpen: Server menu -> Fleet (can also be opened from a label chip). Renders as the FleetPanel tab; it opens its own sessions to each labeled connection and closes them on unmount.
keyActions: Pick a label from the dropdown (only labels naming more than one server qualify)
Re-check (button) - re-run all three checks in one pass
Variables tab - see drifting global variables; toggle 'Include variables expected to differ' (server_id, hostname, read_only, paths...)
Indexes tab - see index divergence with present/missing servers and severity
Statistics tab - see tables whose stats are stale (older than STALE_DAYS) or never measured
fleet.engines: MySQL and PostgreSQL only (gated to sqlDba); Redis connections are excluded from label membership. MySQL uses SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES / information_schema.statistics / mysql.innodb_table_stats; PostgreSQL uses SHOW ALL / pg_indexes / pg_stat_user_tables.
fleet.caveats: Entirely read-only. Requires live connections to at least two reachable members of the label; fewer and it cannot compare. A member that cannot answer a given query is simply absent from that check rather than counted as 'everything missing'. Role detection falls back to 'unknown' for isolated servers.

cluster.summary: Monitor all selected MariaDB Galera or PXC nodes at once. Node cards show state, queues, flow control, write rates, transfers and gcache. Cluster-wide findings identify split-brain, membership disagreement, slow nodes and donor/joiner pairs.
cluster.howToOpen: Server menu -> Galera cluster (also Tools > Server > Galera cluster). Renders as the GaleraClusterPanel tab; it polls SAVED connections, not the session it is open in - the current connection's folder-mates are pre-selected because the nodes of a cluster are usually already one folder.
keyActions: Tick the cluster's nodes in the picker (grouped by folder; the current connection's folder is pre-selected)
Read the cluster-findings banner - split-brain CRIT is unmissable on top
Per node card: state badge, size-as-seen, FC%, queues, commits/s and bytes/s in/out, IST bar / SST transfer card, gcache window
Open (per node) - connect to that node and land on its own Galera tab
Pause/resume the 5s auto-poll; Refresh for a manual round
cluster.engines: MySQL-family with wsrep only (MariaDB Galera Cluster, Percona XtraDB Cluster); the picker lists MySQL-family connections only and the backend skips anything else with a note event.
cluster.caveats: Read-only SHOW probes need no special grant. Poll sessions are ephemeral. Rates and transfer clocks reset when the panel closes; hidden tabs do not poll. Missing keys and dead nodes degrade comparisons, never the whole view.

csvimport.summary: Import CSV, JSON, NDJSON or spreadsheets in three steps: File & target, Columns, Run. Map or skip columns, create or reuse a table, review options, then run transactionally with live byte-based progress.
csvimport.howToOpen: Data menu -> CSV import. Renders as the CsvImportPanel tab with sessionId, engine, environment, and readOnly.
keyActions: Browse... to pick a CSV/TSV/TXT/JSON/NDJSON/JSONL/XLSX/XLSM/XLS/ODS file; pick a sheet for multi-sheet spreadsheets
Choose delimiter and 'first row is header'
Choose 'Into an existing table' or 'Create a new table', and set the table name
Map/skip columns; for new tables edit target column names and types
Options: 'delete existing rows first' (truncate), 'upsert on duplicate key' (MySQL update / PG skip), 'empty cells -> NULL'
Import (button) - streams inserts with a live progress bar and row count; imports are audited
csvimport.engines: MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQLite (gated to csvImport). Upsert wording differs: MySQL ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE vs PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (skip).
csvimport.caveats: Requires write access and is blocked on read-only connections. Prod confirms first, especially when deleting rows. Import is transactional and continues in the backend if the tab closes, with activity and cancellation still visible.

playground.summary: Manufacture real load and lock scenarios for practising Processes, Locks and killall. Choose Sleep mess, Lock storm or Mixed mayhem, review the tagged statement shapes, then spawn and stop real server threads.
playground.howToOpen: Activity menu -> Playground. Renders as the PlaygroundPanel tab with the current session.
keyActions: Pick a scenario card (Sleep mess / Lock storm / Mixed mayhem)
Set parameters: threads, duration, stagger, repeats, jitter %, hold (lock scenarios), database/schema, tag
Read the 'What will run' statement-shape preview
Spawn mess (button) - opens N real server connections/threads running the chosen workload
Stop & kill spawned (button) - end the run and kill the threads it created
Jump to open Processes or open Locks; clear a finished run
playground.engines: MySQL and PostgreSQL only (gated to sqlDba). MySQL uses SLEEP()/SELECT ... FOR UPDATE; PostgreSQL uses pg_sleep() and lock_timeout.
playground.caveats: Spawned threads are real and outlive the panel: closing the tab or app does not stop them. Use Stop or disconnect. Lock/Mixed scenarios write one playground table and need write access; Sleep mess is SELECT-only and works read-only.

quality.summary: Review queries, schemas and migrations before running them. Query mode combines static and server-backed checks; Schema reviews a MySQL catalog; Change review builds sequential and final models for MySQL/MariaDB or PostgreSQL migrations.
quality.howToOpen: SQL menu -> SQL Quality. Renders as the SqlQualityPanel tab with the current session.
keyActions: Switch between Query, Schema and Change review modes
Load .sql... or paste a statement or migration; override the target DB; supply values for ? / :named parameters in Query mode

Pick checks: static lint, column map, InnoDB statistics, referenced tables (sizes+DDL), data-type audit, integer ceilings, EXPLAIN+warnings, EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON, EXPLAIN ANALYZE (with a guard timeout)
Analyze (button) - runs the selected checks; SQL is auto-beautified; pasted CREATE TABLE DDL is routed to a table-design audit
Change review: inspect per-statement and final-model findings with source line/column evidence; optionally seed the before-state from the live catalog
Review schema (button, MySQL) - audit a whole database's catalog
Adjust detail level, severity floor, and 'Passed' toggle; Export .md / raw .txt, Copy, Findings .md/.txt; open raw-output chips (EXPLAIN, DDL, sizes, JSON, ANALYZE)
quality.engines: MySQL and PostgreSQL are server-capable. MySQL adds InnoDB statistics, integer ceilings, index advice and Schema review. Change review supports MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL. SQLite and other engines run offline static lint only.
quality.caveats: Server-backed checks need a live connection. Migration-only Change review works offline; unsupported syntax produces a finding. EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the query with a timeout. Sizes are estimates, and Schema review is MySQL-only.

serverinfo.summary: Search server variables, configuration and status. MySQL uses SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES/STATUS, PostgreSQL uses pg_settings/pg_stat_database, and Redis uses CONFIG/INFO. MySQL and PostgreSQL changes are generated as SQL for review.
serverinfo.howToOpen: Server menu -> Server variables & status. Renders as the ServerInfoPanel tab with sessionId and engine.
keyActions: Toggle Variables/Config vs Status/INFO view
Search across all cells; on PostgreSQL toggle 'changed only'
Refresh the data
Copy/export via the CopyExportMenu

Set... (MySQL/PG) - pick a variable row and generate a review-only SET GLOBAL / ALTER SYSTEM SET (plus SET PERSIST hint on MySQL 8+) inserted into the active editor; PostgreSQL also offers Reset to default (ALTER SYSTEM RESET)
serverinfo.engines: MySQL, PostgreSQL, Redis, ClickHouse (gated to serverInfo). Variable editing (Set...) is available only on MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL.
serverinfo.caveats: Requires a live connection. Generated SET/ALTER statements are never executed by this panel - they are handed to the SQL editor for review and manual running. PG note: ALTER SYSTEM writes postgresql.auto.conf and reloads, but restart-only GUCs still need a restart.

locks.summary: One panel with Blocking and Deadlocks tabs. Follow live blocking chains, inspect a deadlock wait-for graph and victim, and reopen retained incidents. MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server use their native lock and deadlock sources.
locks.howToOpen: Activity menu -> Locks & Deadlocks. Renders as the LocksPanel tab with the session; the Blocking and Deadlocks tabs sit under the toolbar.
keyActions: Blocking tab: view blocking chains (waiting vs blocking pid, wait age, statements, locked table/index or wait event)
Kill the blocker (confirm-gated, audited)
MySQL: browse parsed InnoDB status tabs (transactions, buffer, row ops, semaphores)
Deadlocks tab: read the current deadlock as a wait-for graph, with the cycle and the victim marked
Inspect each edge's lock mode, table and index; view the raw deadlock section behind the parse
Re-open any recorded incident from the local history; delete stored events
PostgreSQL: see per-database deadlock counts and counter-snapshot history
Pause/resume the 5s auto-refresh (Blocking tab)
locks.engines: MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server (gated to lockWaits). The graph is MySQL and SQL Server — see caveats.
locks.caveats: Reads are read-only; Kill is confirmed and audited. Hidden tabs stop polling. PostgreSQL has counters rather than graphs. MySQL exposes only the latest server deadlock, so local history is needed for older incidents.

maintenance.summary: Run table upkeep, find objects broken by schema changes, and perform reviewed bulk edits. Tabs cover Upkeep & invalid objects, Bulk edit and conditional Vacuum advisor; SQLite has a separate whole-file view.
maintenance.howToOpen: Server menu -> Maintenance. Renders as the MaintenancePanel tab (title '🩹 Maintenance') with the current session and selected database; a 'prod' badge shows when the environment is prod.
keyActions: Filter and select tables in the sidebar (all/none); see 'N selected'

Upkeep tab: pick a maintenance operation (engine-specific; destructive ones styled danger and requiring you to type the op name), preview 'N statements for M tables', then Run - EXECUTES via monitor_query with per-table ok/problem results
Scan for invalid objects (read-only probes) - lists broken objects with kind/name/problem/suggested action
Bulk edit tab (MySQL): change a table property (engine/collation/comment) across selected tables; requires typing REBUILD when it rebuilds tables; EXECUTES ALTER statements
Vacuum advisor tab (PostgreSQL): scan pg_stat_user_tables, rank tables by need, offer VACUUM/ANALYZE/REINDEX/VACUUM FULL/CLUSTER actions - these are review-only (emitted to the editor, not executed)
SQLite view: whole-file actions (VACUUM, integrity checks, ANALYZE) with impact badges, tuned by PRAGMA auto_vacuum - these EXECUTE
maintenance.engines: MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQLite (gated to maintenance). MySQL: per-table upkeep + bulk edit (information_schema.TABLES). PostgreSQL: upkeep + Vacuum advisor (bulk edit is empty - a MySQL concept). SQLite: dedicated whole-file view. Engines with no maintenance statements show a note.
maintenance.caveats: Upkeep, Bulk edit and SQLite actions EXECUTE SQL after preview; only Vacuum advisor is review-only. MySQL DDL cannot roll back. Every run is audited. Destructive operations require typed confirmation; failed invalid-object probes are marked partial.

erdiagram.summary: Explore a live schema as a pannable, zoomable foreign-key graph. Focus related tables, adjust density, search columns, save layouts and notes, compare snapshots, and export the diagram. Catalog metadata only; table data is never read.
erdiagram.howToOpen: Schema menu -> ER diagram. Renders as the ErDiagram tab with sessionId, connectionId, and engine (no readOnly/environment - it never writes).
keyActions: Pick a schema; zoom (-, %, +, Fit), Ctrl/Cmd+wheel zoom, drag-to-pan, drag nodes; Auto-arrange
Density 'Show' select (All columns / Keys only / Names only) and colour-by-name-prefix
Search 'Find table or column' and jump to the first hit
Saved diagrams: New/Rename/Delete, persisted per connection; add sticky Notes on an active diagram
Schema-drift: Snapshot a baseline, then Drift toggle highlights added/changed/dropped tables
Export SVG / PNG / Copy image to clipboard

Click a node to focus neighbours; double-click to open in Data Browser; per-table right-click menu (browse, design, add referenced/referencing/neighbours, remove, copy name, insert, select top 100, view DDL)
For FK-poor schemas: 'Read column comments' to discover soft/virtual FKs (drawn dashed), added individually or all
+ Table (design a new table) and a Legend
erdiagram.engines: Gated to erDiagram (mysql, postgres, sqlite per the cap table), but the component's introspection SQL only branches MySQL vs PostgreSQL and its unsupported fallback reads 'ER diagram is available for MySQL and PostgreSQL.' Unsupported: ClickHouse, Redis, Parquet.
erdiagram.caveats: Requires live catalog introspection and is read-only. Virtual FKs, saved diagrams and snapshots are local state. FK-less schemas need column-comment scanning for soft references. The current component targets MySQL/PostgreSQL despite the SQLite capability flag.

datagen.summary: Generate realistic data in three steps: Target, Configure, Preview & Run. Use a schema kit, fill an existing table or design a new one. Preview rows and exact SQL before a chunked insert with progress and ETA.
datagen.howToOpen: Data menu -> Data generator. Renders as the DataGenPanel tab (title '🎲 Data generator') with sessionId, engine, environment, readOnly, connectionName, and schema.
keyActions: Step 1: choose target mode (whole database from a schema kit / fill existing table with 'Load columns' introspection / create new table with inline column design or a chart-shape preset); pick a Locale pack
Step 2 (kit): scale buttons (0.1x-50x), seed + reroll, editable per-table row counts, FK indicators

Step 2 (table): row count + size ladder with byte estimate, seed + reroll, per-column generator picker with contextual params (range, dates, lists/regex, FK parent, decimals, step/jitter, geo, time-series, distribution, % null, unique)
Step 3: preview sample rows (FastGrid) and exact CREATE/INSERT SQL, optional Postgres COPY fast path, then Insert / Create table & insert - streamed with progress, rows/s, ETA, and Cancel
datagen.engines: MySQL and PostgreSQL only (gated to dataGen). Engine differences: Database vs Schema labelling, per-engine identifier quoting, server-side bulk path (PG INSERT...SELECT generate_series or COPY FROM STDIN; MySQL digit-table cross-join). False for ClickHouse, Redis, SQLite, Parquet.
datagen.caveats: Requires a writable MySQL/PostgreSQL connection; other engines are unavailable. Prod confirms first. Step 3 shows SQL but Run really inserts rows. Manual transactions block the server-side path. Runs are audited and can be cancelled after closing the tab.

users.summary: Inspect MySQL accounts or PostgreSQL roles and decode their grants. Create, alter, drop, GRANT and REVOKE are always generated into the editor for deliberate review; the panel never executes a mutation.
users.howToOpen: Server menu -> Users & grants. Renders as the UsersPanel tab (title '👤 Users & grants') with sessionId and engine. MariaDB is detected via an async server-flavor probe.
keyActions: Filter and browse the account/role list; click a row to load its grants (MySQL SHOW GRANTS; PG table-privilege summary)

Create user... / Create role... and Alter/drop... open a lifecycle form (identity, password, auth plugin/attributes, PG role attributes) with a live SQL preview that emits Create/Apply/Drop SQL to the editor
MySQL privilege matrix: pick scope (global/database/table), tick privileges, 'Apply changes -> editor' generates the GRANT/REVOKE diff
MySQL 8 roles section (not MariaDB): create roles, grant to user, set default - all as generated SQL
PostgreSQL: Open Grant Wizard... to decode relacl/nspacl into a grantee x privilege matrix and emit GRANT/REVOKE plus ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES
Grant shortcut templates: grant read/write on a schema, revoke all on a schema
users.engines: MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL only (gated to sqlDba). MySQL reads mysql.user (MariaDB reads mysql.global_priv and surfaces is_role); PostgreSQL reads pg_roles/pg_auth_members and information_schema.table_privileges. Code has only two branches (mysql vs everything-else-as-postgres); no sqlite/clickhouse/redis handling.
users.caveats: Requires a live MySQL/PostgreSQL connection. Every write is review-only, including DROP. Listing needs catalog read privileges; the PG Grant Wizard loads lazily. PG summaries and wizard results are capped. Passwords are never stored or logged.

saved.summary: A local, folder-organized library of reusable SQL. Search folders and names, click to insert SQL, or save the current editor buffer. Positional aliases (:1, :2, …) substitute values when invoked from the editor.
saved.howToOpen: SQL menu -> Saved queries. Renders as the SavedQueriesPanel tab; it takes the current editor buffer (for saving) and inserts selected SQL into the editor.
keyActions: Save current (button) - name + optional folder to save the current editor content
Search saved queries (fuzzy over folder/name)
Click an item to insert its SQL into the editor
Delete a saved query
saved.engines: All engines (no engine gate). Storage is local (app SQLite), independent of the connected engine.
saved.caveats: Save current is disabled when the editor is empty. Storage is local to the app, not the connected database.

history.summary: Search the current connection's locally recorded statements with timestamps, row counts, execution times and errors. Click to reuse SQL, delete one entry, or clear the connection's history after confirmation.
history.howToOpen: Insights menu -> Query history. Renders as the HistoryPanel tab with the connectionId.
keyActions: Filter history (debounced search over stored statements)
Click an entry to load its SQL into the editor
Delete a single history entry
Clear all history for the connection (confirm-gated)
history.engines: All engines (no engine gate). History is stored locally per connection.
history.caveats: Shows locally recorded history for the given connection only; limited to the 200 most recent matching entries.

vacuum.summary: PostgreSQL vacuum and bloat investigations in one place: current vacuum progress, per-table autovacuum backlog, estimated or exact bloat, wraparound risk, and reviewed maintenance actions with lock/cost warnings.
vacuum.howToOpen: Schema menu -> Vacuum & Bloat. Renders as the VacuumBloatPanel tab for the current session. PostgreSQL only — the menu item is greyed with the reason on every other engine.
keyActions: See vacuums in progress, with phase and progress, and what is blocking them
Read the autovacuum backlog ranked against each table's own reloptions threshold
Measure table and index bloat — estimated, or exact where pgstattuple is installed (with a one-click install statement generated, never run)
Check wraparound / freeze age and what is holding the horizon back
Run VACUUM (VERBOSE, ANALYZE), ANALYZE, REINDEX TABLE / INDEX, VACUUM FULL or CLUSTER — each stating its lock level and cost BEFORE it runs, with typed confirmation for the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE rewrites
Send any generated statement to the editor instead of executing it
vacuum.engines: PostgreSQL only (gated on the `postgres` engine, not a capability flag).
vacuum.caveats: Maintenance actions WRITE through an audited path; read-only sessions offer editor SQL instead. Prod hard limits apply to ACCESS EXCLUSIVE rewrites. pg_repack is advice only. Exact pgstattuple scans are capped by relation size.

querystore.summary: Use SQL Server Query Store to find plan regressions, compare every stored plan and review plan forcing. Regressions rank by time wasted, not just ratio. The Forced tab shows pins SQL Server has stopped applying.
querystore.howToOpen: Insights menu -> Query Store. SQL Server only — the entry is absent on engines that keep no plan history. Renders as the QueryStorePanel tab.
keyActions: Find the queries running a worse plan than their best, ranked by the execution time it is costing
Compare every plan a query has had by duration, executions and average logical reads
Open any stored plan's XML in the plan viewer, including the one that is no longer used
Generate sp_query_store_force_plan / sp_query_store_unforce_plan into the editor for review
See every plan already forced, and which forcings SQL Server has silently stopped applying
querystore.engines: SQL Server (2016+). Requires Query Store to be ON for the database.
querystore.caveats: Reading is free; forcing generates SQL into the editor and is never executed by the panel. Empty results distinguish Query Store OFF, READ_ONLY and AUTO capture skipping cheap queries. The Forced tab exposes abandoned or invalid pins.

watch.summary: Three monitoring modes: Metrics charts query values over time; Statement follows live work and watchdog candidates; Wait profile samples PostgreSQL waits. Thread progress for ALTER TABLE and CREATE INDEX opens read-only from Processes.
watch.howToOpen: Activity menu -> Watch (also on the native Tools menu). The read-only Thread progress dialog opens from the Processes panel's '⏱ Progress <id>' button on a selected row.
keyActions: Switch modes: Metrics / Statement / Wait profile (a mode the engine or role cannot serve is greyed with the reason)
Metrics: pick an engine preset or type a query, choose the interval (1-60s), Start/Stop; click a metric card for a full-size history chart
Statement: write a statement and Run - tracks elapsed, phase, progress %; Cancel (KILL) a running watched statement
Statement, pinned: watch a thread started elsewhere read-only; Unpin to return to the editor flow
Statement: Watchdog toggle - full-processlist scan with a seconds threshold; per detected query Kill (audited), Explain (plain, never ANALYZE), Copy
Wait profile (PostgreSQL): choose a sampling interval (100-500 ms), Sample/Stop, read the by-type histogram and by-event breakdown
watch.engines: Metrics: all engines. Statement: MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server (the longQueryWatch capability; the processlist-all privilege, else the mode greys with the reason). Wait profile: PostgreSQL only.
watch.caveats: Watched statements continue on the server when hidden or closed. Pinned-thread watching is read-only; killing stays in Processes. MySQL DDL phases need performance_schema instruments. Hidden tabs pause polling.

timeline.summary: A chronological incident view for one connection and time window. It merges local audit/session events, deadlocks, digest snapshots, fleet runs and long-query captures, with kind filters, day groups and a density strip.
timeline.howToOpen: Insights menu -> Incident timeline (also Tools ▸ Insights ▸ Incident timeline). Renders as the IncidentTimelinePanel tab with the session.
keyActions: Pick a from/to window (datetime-local, defaults to today) and Refresh — no polling
Toggle kind chips (stmt / session / deadlock / snapshot / fleet run / long query) to filter the list
Click a row to expand its detail (full SQL, error text, deadlock victim)
Copy a row's detail, or insert its statement into the editor
timeline.engines: All engines (no engine gate, no privilege gate). Everything shown is local data from history.db — nothing is read from the server.
timeline.caveats: Deadlocks are recorded only while Locks & Deadlocks is open. Store caps mean an empty window can reflect retention rather than a quiet server; the footer names the oldest event. Audit rows use connection names, so renaming orphans older rows.
